articles.title: ‘Try to eat really well, 80% of the time’: nutrition expert says healthy eating is easier than you think
articles.summary: Christopher Gardner, the author of Food Sense and director of nutrition studies at Stanford, says we have overcomplicated the question of what to eat. Finally, some good news: eating well is more straightforward than you think.
body: In the age of social media and wellness grift, we’ve overcomplicated the question of what to eat, he says.

In 2023, Gardner was invited to serve on the US government’s dietary guidelines advisory committee, reviewing the official guidelines for healthy eating and recommending updates. “It was quite an honour to be asked,” remembers Gardner. It was also “a tonne of work”.

Gardner was more than up for the task. He has researched nutrition for more than 30 years, regularly advising official bodies on the latest science and conducting his own gold-standard studies on everything from fermented foods to fish oil.
But when, after two years of work, the committee submitted its 400-page report, it was summarily dismissed by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the Trump administration’s new health secretary, and his team.
points: Christopher Gardner, the author of Food Sense and director of nutrition studies at Stanford, says we have overcomplicated the question of what to eat.

articles.title: I hate golf | Adrian Chiles
articles.summary: I’ve been trying to quit the game for years. Just when I thought I was out, it pulled me back in … I hate golf. A good walk spoiled? The whole day spoiled, more like. As with many cases of hate, it has its roots in love. You see, I just love the feeling of hitting the ball sweetly.
body: My logic ran that if I could play like that as an absolute beginner, imagine what I could do with a bit of practice. I strode up to my ball on the fairway and, swinging with great confidence, played an air shot. Missed it completely. Pretending this was but my practice swing, I tried again, and this time made contact with the ball, but mostly with the ground, causing lasting damage to the fairway. The ball advanced all of six inches. Welcome to golf.

That a complete novice can hit a proper shot is both the best thing about golf and the worst. It draws you in, giving you great encouragement. But it also drives you nuts when, unaccountably, you suddenly can’t do it. Other skills aren’t like this. Take the piano. To play even just the slow opening bit of Beethoven’s Pathétique Sonata would take years of practice. Nobody ever sat at a piano, with no experience, and on day one played anything resembling Beethoven. Yet in golf, it is kind of possible. And it’s equally possible, moments later, to find yourself quite incapable of doing anything of the sort.

articles.title: I went to a Jamaican Patois class. Why was I so scared to speak it?
articles.summary: Centuries of historical baggage surrounds this form of speech. But I’m vowing to overcome shame and connect with this part of my culture. Don’t get The Long Wave delivered to your inbox? Sign up here.
body: Recently, my sister sent me and my mum a graphic promoting a Jamaican Patois (or Patwa) class on Instagram, organised by British teacher and author Naia Lewis. It was unlike anything I’d ever seen before – Patois and other Caribbean Creole forms of speech are rarely treated as legitimate languages.

As a descendant of Caribbean migrants to the UK, I grew up surrounded by Patois, but had never practised speaking it. I wanted to go, but felt terrified of embarrassing myself. This week, I conquered that fear and explored why learning Patois and other Creole languages is so fraught and controversial across the diaspora.

articles.title: I spent months taste-testing 15 tinned fish varieties. These are the ones I’d eat again
articles.summary: Is it possible to get tired of eating tinned fish? From Fishwife tuna to Wildfish salmon, I ate tinned fish 15 different ways. The 10 best (and worst) whey protein powders – taste-tested. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: A s a child, I often wrinkled my nose at the humble cans of anchovies and salmon that my grandparents diligently stocked in their pantry, wondering why they would choose a cold chunk instead of a freshly baked fillet. But in recent years, tinned fish has undergone a facelift. The pungent anchovies people have avoided like the plague are now a coveted consumable.

While tinned fish has been around for ages, its popularity is a relatively recent phenomenon. Brands such as Fishwife, launched in 2020, have turned conservas into a status symbol, collaborating with chains such as Sweetgreen and celebrities such as gen-Z musician Audrey Hobert. More unique offerings such as oysters and mackerel have entered the mainstream too.

“There are all these cool brands now that are so easy to find in grocery stores. I think that has urged people to be more curious and give it a try,” says Anna Hezel, the author of Tin to Table, a cookbook featuring more than 50 ways to eat tinned fish.

articles.title: How to Style a Leather Jacket for Fall
articles.summary: From oversized motos to fitted zip-ups, the current forecast is prime leather weather.
body: Leather jackets have long been the go-to cool-girl signifier, so it’s no surprise that come fashion week, they’re all over the street style circuit. There’s a reason we get excited for fall–or, more specifically, leather weather. Few pieces have quite the same ability to make an outfit feel instantly cooler.

These days, there’s a leather jacket for nearly every mood. Oversized bombers and close-fitting cropped styles mingle with polished trenches, slouchy anoraks, and classic motos. The styling possibilities are just as varied. Go the model-off-duty route with lived-in denim and a knit, or use a leather jacket to toughen up polished separates like tailored trousers and a blouse. You can even follow Mrs. Prada’s lead and play with contrast, throwing one over a printed dress or skirt.
When it comes to fall style, a great leather jacket does much of the work for you. Here are six ways we’re wearing them now.
A rich brown leather jacket adds an element of cool to tailored black trousers. Keep the accessories sleek and minimal with a structured bag and barely-there flats.
points: From oversized motos to fitted zip-ups, the current forecast is prime leather weather.

articles.title: Doom and Disillusionment, Meet Fontaines D.C.’s ‘Dopamine Chamber’
articles.summary: Vogue sits down with Grian Chatten and Carlos O’Connell of the Grammy-nominated Fontaines D.C. to discuss their forthcoming fifth album, “Dopamine Chamber.”
body: With its pulsing bass and Lynchian music video, “ Marianne ”—the lead single from Fontaines D.C.’s fifth album, Dopamine Chamber —offered both a thrilling sign of things to come and compelling proof of just how much they had evolved from the gritty guitars and half-spoken-word vocals of their 2019 debut, Dogrel.

Of course, not everything has changed. The members of Fontaines D.C.—namely, lead vocalist Grian Chatten, guitarists Conor Curley and Carlos O’Connell, bassist Conor “Deego” Deegan III, and drummer Tom Coll—have always been a cerebral bunch, as uncompromising in their creative vision as their politics, even as their audience has ballooned. When I meet with Chatten and O’Connell at their Brooklyn hotel in mid-September, their humility is still intact, too. The success of their last album, the Grammy-nominated Romance (2024), cemented the Irish band’s shift from breakthrough act to global headliners.

articles.title: Wildfires Are Sweeping Across Peru’s Cusco Region: What Travelers Should Know
articles.summary: From air quality concerns to exact areas impacted, here's the 411.
body: In Peru’s mountainous southern region, dozens of wildfires have destroyed tens of thousands of acres of land in the past few weeks and left at least five people dead.

Although this region regularly sees wildfires, the blazes this fall have been more intense and dangerous than usual. “Wildfires in the Cusco region occur regularly when farmers clear their land in preparation for the next planting season and strong winds cause the fires to spread beyond control,” says Pedro Barraza, managing director of South America at andBeyond.

In 2026, higher-than-normal temperatures and drier conditions in Peru’s Andean highlands caused by El Niño have shifted “the timing and behavior of seasonal wildfires,” according to Barraza, making them more difficult to control than usual.

Local authorities are sending firefighters, army personnel, and a specialized water plane to the region in hope of containing the quickly spreading flames, according to Peru’s agricultural minister on X, though residents and social media users say the response has been slow.

articles.title: The Best Costa Rica Airbnbs Near Cloud Forests, Surf Breaks, and Towering Volcanoes
articles.summary: Stunning homes for solo travelers, large groups, and everyone in between.
body: From misty cloud forests and abundant biodiversity to tucked-away waterfalls and some of the world’s top surf breaks, Costa Rica is the ultimate destination for the adventurous traveler. But in this Central American country, big adventures don’t mean sacrificing thoughtful accommodations. And there are plenty of spectacular Airbnbs in Costa Rica that put guests in the perfect location to explore all the beauty this country has to offer.

In Tamarindo, expansive villas designed for indoor-outdoor living sit within walking distance of the area’s golden beaches and surf breaks. In Monteverde, cozy one-bedroom cabins offer a front-row seat to the diverse wildlife in the country’s cloud forest region. And in San Cayetano de Venecia, near the Arenal Volcano, travelers interested in regenerative agriculture can stay on a working dairy farm amid miles of rolling pastures where cows graze.

articles.title: My Ride-or-Die Beauty Products Are Travel-Friendly and Completely Leakproof
articles.summary: From a long-lasting perfume oil to a spill-proof foundation, these compact beauty finds never let me down.
body: Traveling with perfume can truly be a recipe for disaster. Fragrance bottles are usually quite delicate, and if your suitcase takes a wrong turn or tumble, everything near that bottle is ruined (and so is your expensive perfume). Not to mention, most perfume packaging is far from compact—which is fine when it's sitting on your vanity, but not so much when it's weighing down your toiletry bag. Even the travel-size bottles of most fragrances are made of glass and are very fragile, so while they’ll easily slide into a small pocket of your weekender bag, they still run the risk of shattering.

My previous gripe with perfume oils was that they weren’t as long-lasting as a spray. Cyklar’s Perfume Oil has completely changed my perspective: The smell remains strong even after hours and hours of wear, and two of the bottles fit in the palm of my hand, making them about an eighth of the size of a normal perfume bottle. I think I have a different scent (all terrific!) in every one of my travel bags. The bottles are made of glass, but they’re very sturdy; I have dropped them a few times and left them loose in my personal item without a single issue.
points: From a long-lasting perfume oil to a spill-proof foundation, these compact beauty finds never let me down.

articles.title: It’s Not a Whitehead, It’s Milia—Here's How to Treat It
articles.summary: Milia isn’t harmful—but some people still want to get rid of it. Here’s what dermatologists suggest to prevent (and treat) the stubborn white bumps. No popping allowed!
body: It’s easy to mistake them for whiteheads: small, pale bumps that crop up overnight, clustered under the eyes, on the cheeks, or along the nose. But before you pick up your tweezers or get to squeezing them (bad!), listen up—what looks like a mild breakout or whiteheads could actually be milia, a completely different kind of skin concern that won’t respond to your tried-and-true acne spot treatment, and definitely not to squeezing.

“Milia are tiny cysts that sit just under the skin’s surface,” explains cosmetic physician and head of education at Acquisition Aesthetics Emmaline Ashley, MD. “They are full of a protein called keratin, which is commonly found in your hair, nails, and the outer layer of skin.” Milia presents itself as pearly white bumps; however, they are not inflammatory, infectious, or even remotely related to acne.

Whiteheads are a type of acne lesion caused by clogged pores that are filled with sebum, dead skin, and bacteria. “Milia, however, are firmer, deeper-set, and won’t extract easily like a whitehead,” warns Dr. Ashley.
points: Milia isn’t harmful—but some people still want to get rid of it.
